sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance that can never be duplicated or replaced, existing for the entire lifetime of the program.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness expressed not through metaphor but through a language guarantee: there will only ever be one.

sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining silently returns nil when any link in the chain is absent, collapsing an entire sequence of hope into nothing without error or complaint.
sketches.resonance: Each `?.` is a question asked knowing it may dissolve — reaching through absence after absence, never arriving.

sketches.mechanism: A value moved into a closure can never be accessed by the original owner — Rust's ownership transfer makes the original binding permanently invalid.
sketches.resonance: Giving yourself to someone means the person you were before can no longer be reached — the compiler enforces the irreversibility of devotion.
